HPC-MIX Bench | Explore precision with confidence

MIXED-PRECISION RESEARCH · NUMERICAL BENCHMARKS

A practical testbed for discovering where lower precision is useful, checking whether the requested accuracy survives, and studying what those choices mean on real workloads.

HPC-MIX Bench brings together C/C++ applications, PROMISE precision search, CADNA-based numerical validation, one-bit format sweeps, and selected H100 CUDA experiments. It connects a variable-level precision assignment to evidence about numerical behavior, search effort, memory, and execution.

Get started · Learn precision tuning · Choose a benchmark

40+

Numerical and machine-learning workloads

4

Standard precision search spaces

1–10

Requested significant-digit targets

CPU + H100

Search artifacts and selected CUDA validation

What can you do with the suite?

Find precision headroom

Compare E4M3 and E5M2, FP16 and BF16, plus FP32 and FP64. Inspect the precision selected for each annotated variable as the required number of correct digits rises. Understand the search.

Study different numerical structures

Test iterative solvers, factorization, interpolation, stencils, and machine-learning kernels. Use contrasting workloads to examine where a tuning method succeeds or becomes conservative. Browse the workloads.

Connect accuracy to hardware behavior

Explore one-bit format sensitivity and selected H100 ports with measured time, tracked device allocation, and error fields. Read the results.

The precision-tuning path

01 · Define accuracy

Pick an application input and the number of correct significant digits that its checked outputs must retain.

02 · Search assignments

PROMISE transforms annotated variables, compiles candidates, and tests lower-precision combinations against its CADNA-based reference.

03 · Inspect the result

Review variable assignments, failed cases, search wall time, and the benchmark-specific output checks before drawing conclusions.

04 · Validate performance

Compare generated implementations with an appropriate FP64 baseline on the target hardware. Keep search time separate from kernel time.

Note

CPU PROMISE plots measure precision-search wall time, including compilation and candidate runs. They do not measure native FP8 hardware throughput. Selected H100 artifacts provide separate execution and allocation measurements. See Benchmark Methodology and Value for the measurement model.
